# Welcome {.unnumbered}
:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="65%"}
<div style="text-align: justify">

**Graphical Modelling and Causal Inference (GMCI)** is an open, 
community-driven resource for researchers working at the intersection 
of graphical models, causal discovery, and statistical methodology. 

We curate FAIR — Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable — 
datasets and executable analysis notebooks, and make them available 
to the broader research community through a moderated 
[Zenodo community](https://zenodo.org/communities/mardigmci).

</div>
:::

::: {.column width="10%"}
:::

::: {.column width="25%"}
![](images/GMCI.png){fig-align="right" width="100%"}
:::

::::

Whether you are looking to benchmark a new algorithm, explore curated datasets, or share your own reproducible analysis, GMCI offers the infrastructure to do so.

## Our Principles {.unnumbered}

GMCI is built on the [FAIR principles](https://fairsharing.org/) for scientific data management [@Wilkinson2016]:

- **Findable** — All resources are indexed with persistent identifiers (DOIs) via Zenodo.
- **Accessible** — Resources are openly available and licensed for reuse where possible.
- **Interoperable** — Datasets follow standardised metadata schemas; notebooks use open, reproducible formats.
- **Reusable** — Clear licensing and provenance information accompany every submission.

## Getting Started {.unnumbered}

New to GMCI? Here is how to get the most out of this resource:

1. **Explore** existing datasets and notebooks to find resources relevant to your research.
2. **Run** a notebook directly — all submissions are archived with reproducible environments on Zenodo.
3. **Contribute** your own dataset or analysis notebook using our [submission guidelines](chapters/contribute.qmd).
4. **Cite** resources you use — each Zenodo record provides a ready-made citation.

## Citation {.unnumbered}

If you use GMCI resources in your work, please cite the curated content's original creators as well as the GMCI community itself:

```bibtex
@article{Mareis_Haug_Drton_2025,
  title   = {MaRDI's Zenodo Community for Graphical Modeling and Causal Inference},
  volume  = {2},
  journal = {Proceedings of the Conference on Research Data Infrastructure},
  author  = {Mareis, Leopold and Haug, Stephan and Drton, Mathias},
  year    = {2025},
  month   = {Sep.}
}
```

→ [Full citation guidance and BibTeX](chapters/about.qmd#citation)
